Zcash’s CPI Selloff Reveals a Deeper Problem for ZEC
selected.description: ZECs latest decline has erased much of its recent consolidation, leaving the recovery from Octobers correction increasingly vulnerable. Futures trading volume increased even as dollar-denominated open interest contracted, pointing to heavy turnover during the selloff. Long liquidations dominated for...
selected.content: ZEC’s latest decline has erased much of its recent consolidation, leaving the recovery from October’s correction increasingly vulnerable. Futures trading volume increased even as dollar-denominated open interest contracted, pointing to heavy turnover during the selloff. Long liquidations dominated forced closures, while slightly negative funding suggests bearish positioning had not reached an extreme. Zcash (ZEC) plunged 10.37% to $1,042.09 on November 10, breaking a key technical level as traders reduced leveraged exposure amid a broader cryptocurrency selloff. The decline followed stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data, which pressured Bitcoin and other major cryptocurrencies. ZEC’s losses were considerably sharper than Bitcoin’s, while derivatives statistics showed a simultaneous contraction in outstanding exposure and an increase in trading activity. The combination points to a market undergoing a rapid repricing after its October rally, with recent buyers facing mounting losses as the cryptocurrency struggles to establish support. Inflation Shock Hits an Already Weak Zcash Market October’s U.S. Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% month over month, exceeding the 0.3% consensus forecast. Core inflation remained persistent, complicating expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts. Bitcoin fell below $74,000 as the broader cryptocurrency market weakened. Privacy-focused Monero (XMR) also declined, placing Zcash’s selloff within a wider retreat from risk rather than an isolated token-specific event. The decline also followed Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade. Although the protocol change provides relevant fundamental context, the available evidence points more directly to broader market weakness and leveraged selling than to a newly identified network failure. ZEC Breaks Its Medium-Term Trend Zcash’s latest decline has weakened its broader technical structure, with selling pressure extending beyond the immediate reaction to the U.S. inflation report. The Coinbase ZEC/USD daily chart shows the price falling below its 100-day simple moving average (SMA) at $1,074.60. Zcash breaks below its 100-day moving average as RSI signals weakening momentum. Source: TradingView, chart by Alexander Zdravkov. The November 10 candle opened at $1,162.14, reached $1,198.71 and subsequently fell to $992.88 before recovering part of the decline. That intraday rebound kept the observed price above the psychological $1,000 threshold, but the sharp rejection from higher levels left a bearish daily candle. The broader chart shows repeated failures to sustain advances toward the upper boundary of the recent consolidation range. Those unsuccessful recovery attempts preceded the latest breakdown and indicate that buyers had been losing control of the market structure. The 14-day Relative Strength Index (RSI) fell to 37.50, below its RSI moving average of 49.11. Momentum remains bearish, although the indicator has yet to reach the conventional oversold threshold of 30. That distinction is important after a double-digit decline. Weak momentum does not automatically imply an imminent rebound, particularly when the price is trading beneath a major trend average. Technical Levels / ZEC-USD Zcash Price Structure Daily chart · November 10, 2026 Overhead Resistance $1,350–$1,370 Repeated rejection zone MAJOR $1,289.09 50-day simple moving average 50 SMA $1,160–$1,170 Former support area PIVOT $1,074.60 Broken medium-term trend 100 SMA Observed ZEC Price $1,042.09 Daily Change -10.37% Downside Support $970–$1,000 Nearest demand area NEAR $810 Lower horizontal support LOWER $782.36 Long-term trend reference 200 SMA Rising Futures Volume Masks a Shrinking Market According to Coinglass, Zcash recorded $9.27 billion in 24-hour futures turnover, an increase of 10.07%, while open interest declined 11.50% to $2.27 billion. The divergence is significant. Trading activity accelerated even as the dollar value of outstanding contracts contracted, indicating that the selloff involved substantial position turnover rather than a straightforward expansion of speculative exposure. One qualification matters: open interest is denominated in dollars. A falling token price reduces the reported notional value of outstanding contracts even without an equivalent reduction in contract quantities. The percentage decline therefore cannot be attributed entirely to traders closing positions. Contract-denominated open interest would provide a clearer measure of actual exposure reduction. Reported futures turnover was approximately 14.6 times spot trading volume, which stood at $636.45 million. The comparison highlights derivatives-market activity, although the two measures represent different trading structures and should not be interpreted as equivalent capital flows. Over the preceding 24 hours, liquidations totaled $33.05 million. Long positions accounted for approximately 90%, equivalent to roughly $29.75 million. Despite those forced closures, perpetual funding remained only slightly negative at -0.0009%. That relatively modest funding imbalance suggests the market had not developed an extreme short-side bias at the time of the snapshot. Heavy long liquidations alongside subdued funding are more consistent with a leveraged position unwind than with evidence of an overwhelming buildup of new bearish exposure. Confirming the balance between long closures and fresh short positions would require additional trade-level data and contract-denominated open interest. What Zcash Needs for a Sustainable Recovery Zcash’s immediate technical bias remains bearish following the breakdown of its medium-term trend. The intraday recovery from below $1,000 demonstrates that buyers were active at lower prices, but it has not repaired the preceding sequence of lower highs. A more convincing recovery requires stronger spot demand and evidence that derivatives exposure has stabilized. Renewed price gains accompanied by rapidly expanding leverage would leave ZEC vulnerable to another round of forced selling. The relationship between price and open interest will help distinguish genuine accumulation from a temporary derivatives-driven rebound. For now, the combination of weakening technical momentum, concentrated long liquidations and contracting dollar-denominated open interest favors a defensive interpretation of the market structure. The next meaningful change would be sustained buying strong enough to reverse the recent breakdown without relying on another expansion in vulnerable leveraged positions. selected.headline: Bitcoin Faces a Tougher Rate Outlook After US October Inflation Rises 0.4%
selected.description: October US CPI rose 0.4% month on month and core CPI increased 0.3%. The hotter reading strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. For…
selected.content: The latest US inflation report has given Bitcoin traders a fresh reason to watch the bond market rather than just the crypto charts. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on November 10 that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% monthly increase economists had broadly expected. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3%. The headline figure slowed from September’s 0.6% increase but still points to inflation pressures that the Federal Reserve cannot easily ignore. TL;DR: October US CPI rose 0.4% month on month and core CPI increased 0.3%. The hotter reading strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy. For Bitcoin, the immediate transmission mechanism runs through interest-rate expectations, the dollar, liquidity and risk appetite—not a mechanical relationship between CPI and BTC. Why a monthly CPI number matters so much A quarter-point difference in inflation might sound small, yet markets were positioned around a particular expectation. When the result is higher than forecast, investors must reconsider how soon the Fed can relax policy, or whether further tightening is required. Higher Treasury yields can make cash and government securities more attractive relative to assets that offer no contractual income, including Bitcoin. The BLS report is also unusual because it does not include a year-on-year October CPI rate. Data-collection disruptions during the federal shutdown in October 2025 left the agency without the normal comparison base. Readers should not fill that gap with an invented annual figure or compare an unofficial estimate with an official monthly release. Shelter costs increased 0.3% and accounted for more than 30% of October’s monthly rise, while food increased 0.5% and energy 0.7%. Bitcoin’s sensitivity is about financial conditions Bitcoin does not have a fixed reaction function to inflation. Some investors describe it as protection against monetary debasement, while others trade it as a high-volatility risk asset. Both descriptions can influence positioning, sometimes on the same day. A surprise that pushes real yields higher can pressure speculative positions even when the longer-run inflation-hedge narrative remains intact. The distinction is especially relevant after recent fund withdrawals. Our report on November 6 Bitcoin ETF outflows explains why heavy selling through listed funds can complicate a market already reacting to macro news. ETF redemptions, however, are not the same thing as every Bitcoin holder exiting. There is a corporate dimension too. Firms that finance Bitcoin positions with equity, debt or preferred shares may find the price of capital changes when bond yields rise. NewsBTC recently examined how Strategy combined a Bitcoin purchase with preferred-share repurchases. Those funding mechanics deserve attention when monetary policy becomes less forgiving. The next signals to check The market will now weigh Fed commentary, Treasury yields and subsequent employment and inflation releases. Traders should also distinguish a brief reaction to the 8:30 a.m. US data release from a sustained change in price direction; crypto trades continuously while other asset markets open and close on different clocks. A higher-than-expected CPI reading is a real headwind for hopes of an imminent policy pivot. It is not a price target for Bitcoin. The stronger editorial conclusion is that the investment environment just became more demanding, particularly for leveraged traders who need both stable financing conditions and rising asset prices. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
